question: There are many two-digit multiples of \(7,\) but only two of the multiples have a digit sum of \(10.\) The sum of these two multiples of \(7\) is
solution:
List the multiples of \(7\) in increasing order. The two-digit multiples begin at \(7\cdot2=14\) and end at \(7\cdot14=98\), since the neighboring multiples are \(7\) and \(105\). The complete list is
\[
\begin{gathered}
14,21,28,35,42,49,56,\\
63,70,77,84,91,98.
\end{gathered}
\]
Only \(28\) and \(91\) have digits summing to \(10\). Their sum is
\[
28+91=\boxed{119},
\]
choice \(\mathrm{A}\).

A factor and a multiple are defined through a product a×b=c. Finding factor pairs and listing multiples both presuppose understanding what a multiplication equation states.
